Ran the hybrid query plus combined OR queries for prius|leaf|volt|ct200h|niro|ioniq|insight|c-max and for the efficient-gas models.

Logged in and searched. The /marketplace/vehicles endpoint worked far better than /search; note FB returned the same ~20-item pool regardless of query term. Photo URLs are signature-signed and were omitted rather than saved broken.
Cheapest hybrid nationally is about $24,590 and cheapest car of any fuel about $14,590. Nothing under $10,000.
Buy-It-Now search returned results but zero within Colorado - all were Florida, New Jersey and similar. Nothing inside the 100-mile radius.
Prius query returned 11 local listings; most are high-mileage.
Only two sub-$10k cars nationally - a 2019 Leaf SL at $6,999 and a 2021 EcoSport at $8,599 - both in Inglewood CA, 854 miles away with about $1,858 delivery. Nothing local.
Searched Denver/Thornton. Cheapest local inventory is about $17,898; their lowest published price band is Under $20k. No sub-$10k cars this run.
Loaded and confirmed 32 Prius listings under $10k, but all are Utah, roughly 450+ miles from 80015. Excluded on distance - local supply was strong enough this run not to need the stretch.

listings.carSeatNotes: Tall-roof compact wagon: easy overhead clearance when lifting a rear-facing seat in, upright rear bench, hatch swallows a stroller plus daycare bags.
listings.nextAction: Dealer listing 13 mi away - ask for the free Carfax and proof the hybrid battery has never thrown a code; then book a test drive.
listings.why: Best all-round pick this run. 40 mpg combined, only 85k miles, CarGurus flags it Great Deal, and it is the newest non-suspect hybrid under $8.5k inside 15 miles. Ford's hybrid transaxle here is the eCVT design with a strong reliability record.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan with a genuinely wide rear bench and easy-to-reach LATCH anchors; verify front-passenger legroom once a rear-facing seat is installed behind it.
listings.nextAction: Ask whether Hyundai's 10yr/100k powertrain warranty transferred or has lapsed, and get the recall-completion printout for the 3 open campaigns.
listings.why: Newest car on the whole list at 6 years old with under 60k miles. 36 mpg combined beats every other gas car here, and Hyundai's 2020 Elantra has a clean reliability record. Cheapest cost-per-mile of any non-hybrid.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan - the roomiest rear seat in the top five. A rear-facing convertible fits without pushing the front passenger seat forward.
listings.nextAction: Great Deal rating plus 5-star NHTSA - move fast. Ask the dealer to confirm the traction battery warranty status (Hyundai covered it 10yr/100k, so it may have just expired).
listings.why: The family-friendly pick: 5-star overall crash rating, 40 mpg combined, and a full midsize back seat for under $9.5k. Hyundai's parallel hybrid uses a conventional 6-speed automatic rather than a CVT, which simplifies long-term repair.

listings.carSeatNotes: Hatchback with a flat rear floor and wide door opening - good for leaning in with a child. Cargo area is shallow but deep enough for a stroller.
listings.nextAction: Ask for a LeafSpy battery-health report (bars remaining and SOH percent) before driving out. A 2017 with 10+ bars easily covers the 25-mile daycare-and-Sam's-Club loop.
listings.why: Cheapest credible car on the list and the running cost is close to zero: your 25-mile workday is a fraction of even a degraded 2017 Leaf's range, and Level 1 charging overnight is plenty. 2017 is the last of the 30 kWh cars, well past the worst battery-degradation years.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan, roomy rear bench and easy LATCH access - one of the better car-seat fits here.
listings.nextAction: Private seller - ask for the VIN and a photo of the title before driving out, then confirm the one-owner claim on a Carfax and check for traction-battery service history.
listings.why: Lowest miles per dollar of any hybrid on the list: 82,500 miles for $7,000 with a one-owner claim. 5-star crash rating and a real midsize back seat. Private sale means room to negotiate, but also means you verify everything yourself.

listings.carSeatNotes: Full midsize rear seat - the easiest rear-facing install on this list, with wide doors for buckling a toddler in a tight parking spot.
listings.nextAction: Only 4 miles away - go see it. Ask for hybrid battery cooling-fan service history (the intake vent behind the rear seat clogs with dust and is the main Camry Hybrid failure mode).
listings.why: The safest bet on the list for a family car. Toyota's hybrid system is the most proven one built, 40 mpg combined, 5-star crash rating, and it is 4 miles from home. Price is at the top of budget but 112k miles is mid-life for this drivetrain.

listings.carSeatNotes: Same flat-floor hatchback layout as the other Leafs; SL trim adds heated rear seats, which matter on a Colorado winter daycare run.
listings.nextAction: Closest car on the list - 7 miles. Ask for a LeafSpy readout; a 2015 with fewer than 10 bars is not worth $8,840.
listings.why: Lowest-mileage Leaf inside 10 miles and an SL, so it has the heated seats and steering wheel that make short winter trips cheap (cabin heat is the main range drain). Priced above the 2017 though, so only take it if the battery health checks out better.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan with the largest back seat and trunk of any gas car here - the most comfortable option for a rear-facing seat plus a stroller.
listings.nextAction: Ask for the CVT service history; the 2020 Malibu's continuously variable transmission is the one component worth a pre-purchase inspection.
listings.why: Newest, roomiest gas car under $10k and just clears the 32 mpg floor. Only 50k miles and a single open recall. Take this over the Elantra if back-seat space matters more than fuel economy.

listings.carSeatNotes: Flat-floor hatchback, wide rear doors; SL trim's heated rear seats help on cold mornings.
listings.nextAction: Lowest miles of any car on the list. Worth the 36-mile drive to Boulder, but get a LeafSpy battery report first so the trip is not wasted.
listings.why: Only 37,994 miles - by far the lowest on this list. A 2016 SL is a 30 kWh car, so real-world range should still comfortably cover the daily loop. Marked only Fair Deal because Leaf pricing has softened, so there is negotiating room.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan; rear bench is adequate for one rear-facing seat but the front passenger will need the seat moved forward.
listings.nextAction: 5-star crash rating at 60k miles. Ask for records on the 1.4T's cooling system - water-outlet and thermostat-housing leaks are the known weak point.
listings.why: 34 mpg combined, 5-star NHTSA overall, 60k miles and 11 miles away. Strong value; the only caveat is the 1.4 turbo's coolant-leak history, which is cheap to fix if caught early.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan with a roomy rear seat; the hybrid battery sits behind the seatback so the trunk is shallower than the gas Fusion - check that your stroller fits.
listings.nextAction: Also listed on CarGurus at the same price. 9 open recall campaigns for this model year - get the completion printout from Ford before anything else.
listings.why: Under $7k for a 38 mpg midsize hybrid with only 91,747 miles and a Great Deal rating. The nine open recalls and the 54-mile drive to Colorado Springs are the reasons it is not higher.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan with a usefully wide rear door aperture; standard AWD means less drama getting out of an unplowed daycare lot.
listings.nextAction: 5 open recalls - get the completion records. Also ask whether it has EyeSight (auto emergency braking); the 2018 base 2.0i often does not.
listings.why: Only car on the list that pairs a 5-star crash rating with standard all-wheel drive, and it still clears the 32 mpg floor. 46k miles at 8 years old is very low. Best choice if Colorado winters worry you more than fuel cost.

listings.carSeatNotes: Tall wagon body, easy overhead clearance for lifting a car seat; the plug-in battery eats trunk depth, so measure before committing to a big stroller.
listings.nextAction: A ~20-mile electric range roughly covers your daily loop on Level 1 charging alone. Ask for the 8 recall completions and a battery state-of-health check.
listings.why: Plug-in that could run your commute almost entirely on electricity while keeping a gas engine for road trips - the best of both for this use case. 102k miles and a 47-mile drive to see it are the trade-offs.

listings.carSeatNotes: Flat-floor hatchback with wide rear doors; base S trim has no heated seats, so winter range will suffer more than the SL cars.
listings.nextAction: Ask for a LeafSpy battery report and confirm whether it is the 24 kWh or 30 kWh pack before making a 54-mile drive to Colorado Springs.
listings.why: Cheap EV miles at $6,495. Ranked below the other Leafs because it is a base S (no heated seats) and 54 miles away, which makes verifying battery health before travelling essential.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan; single rear-facing seat fits, but check front-passenger clearance once installed.
listings.nextAction: Great Deal at 55 miles out - call first and ask them to email the Carfax and confirm it is still on the lot before driving to Colorado Springs.
listings.why: 33 mpg, 5-star crash rating and a Great Deal tag at just over $8k with 70k miles. The 55-mile distance is the only real knock.

listings.carSeatNotes: Sentra has an unusually large back seat for a compact - noticeably easier for a rear-facing install than a Civic or Corolla of the same era.
listings.nextAction: Ask for CVT fluid-change records; Nissan's Xtronic CVT is the one thing that decides whether this car is a bargain or a headache.
listings.why: Also on Craigslist at the same price. Great Deal rating, 32 mpg, class-leading rear-seat room, 19 miles away. Rated below the newer gas cars purely because of the CVT's reputation.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact - the tightest car-seat fit on this list. Install a rear-facing seat and check the front passenger still has usable legroom before you commit.
listings.nextAction: Best fuel economy of any gas-burning car here. Ask for hybrid battery diagnostics given 116k miles, and bring your actual car seat to the test drive.
listings.why: 50 mpg combined and Toyota hybrid reliability for under $8k, 8 miles away. Ranked here rather than higher only because the c is a subcompact and rear-seat space is genuinely tight with a rear-facing seat.

listings.carSeatNotes: Full midsize rear seat, very easy rear-facing install; the plug-in battery cuts trunk space to about 10 cubic feet, so a bulky stroller may be a squeeze.
listings.nextAction: Also on CarGurus at $8,694 - use the lower Cars.com price as your anchor. A 29-mile electric range covers your whole daily loop on a regular outlet.
listings.why: Newest plug-in on the list and the only one whose electric range fully covers the 25-mile workday. 5-star crash rating and a midsize back seat. The 127k miles is the reason it is not top five.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan, generous rear seat and wide doors - a comfortable rear-facing install.
listings.nextAction: Only 6 miles away and it has been listed for weeks - reasonable room to negotiate. Ask about hybrid starter-generator belt service.
listings.why: Still live from previous runs at the same $7,350. 89k miles, 37 mpg, 5-star crash rating and the second-closest car on the list. Kia's hybrid is less proven than Toyota's, which caps how high it should rank.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan with a roomy back seat; hybrid battery reduces trunk depth versus the gas Fusion, so measure your stroller.
listings.nextAction: 13 open recall campaigns for this model year - demand the completion printout before anything else. Posted twice by the same dealer, so treat the second ad as a repost, not a second car.
listings.why: Highest EPA rating of any conventional hybrid here at 41 mpg combined, with a 5-star crash rating and under 100k miles. Top of budget, and the recall count is the highest on the list.

listings.carSeatNotes: Only four seats - the rear has two buckets split by a battery tunnel. One car seat fits fine; a second child later would not.
listings.nextAction: 5 miles away and a 38-mile electric range covers your commute twice over. Ask for a battery capacity readout and confirm the 8yr/100k battery warranty status.
listings.why: Longest electric range of any plug-in here and a single open recall. 5-star crash rating, 5 miles from home. The four-seat layout and 100k miles are the limiting factors.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact - tight for a rear-facing seat. Bring the seat to the viewing and check front-passenger legroom.
listings.nextAction: Private seller in Aurora - ask for the VIN and a photo of the title before meeting, and arrange the handover somewhere public.
listings.why: Newer than the 2014 Prius c at a lower price, right in Aurora, 50 mpg. Listed since mid-July without selling, so the asking price has room. Same subcompact rear-seat caveat applies.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan with a snug rear seat - workable for one rear-facing seat but tighter than the Sentra or Elantra.
listings.nextAction: Mileage was not shown on the listing - confirm the odometer reading before anything else, then ask for the Carfax.
listings.why: 33 mpg, 5-star crash rating, and Mazda's naturally aspirated 2.0 Skyactiv is one of the most trouble-free engines of its era. Ranked here only because the listing did not disclose mileage.

listings.carSeatNotes: Four seats only, with two rear buckets separated by the battery tunnel. Fine for one child, no room to grow.
listings.nextAction: Price dropped from $5,500 to $3,999 - ask why, and get the VIN plus a title photo before viewing. Have the battery capacity checked; a degraded 2012 pack is the likely reason for the discount.
listings.why: Cheapest plug-in by a wide margin after a $1,500 price cut, and a 35-mile electric range would cover the daily loop. The steep drop and missing mileage mean this needs careful verification before it deserves a higher rank.

listings.carSeatNotes: Hatchback with a usable rear bench and a large cargo hold - genuinely practical for daycare runs if the car is real.
listings.nextAction: TREAT AS SUSPECT. A 2022 Prius Prime with 62k miles is a $22k-$25k car; $8,450 is far below any plausible market price. Price just dropped again from $8,950. Do not wire a deposit, do not accept a shipping story - insist on seeing the car and title in person in Denver, and walk away if the seller resists.
listings.why: Carried over from previous runs and the price dropped $500 this week. On paper it is the best car on the list - 54 mpg, 5-star, 2022. In practice the price is roughly a third of market, which is the classic signature of a fraudulent listing. Listed for transparency, not as a recommendation.
